notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], stretch_mujoco/models/scene.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; the bridge derives one control interval per actuator from the loaded model's actuator_ctrlrange and checks every element before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The scene includes stretch.xml and docking_station.xml (scene.xml:2-3), so the served world contains the robot, the docking station and the scene's table and free objects. The card's other models, stretch.xml and stretch_mj_3.3.0.xml, are not served separately: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card's family-config/MujocoDriver decision matches the upstream, a MuJoCo simulation stack for Stretch (README.md:11,101-107; mujoco_server.py:248-258) whose default scene is models/scene.xml (utils.py:33-34). MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (the form the SDK's own MujocoDriver tests use). The lock names it .fake:FakeMujoco. The stand-in expands the scene's includes, resolves the MJCF default classes (including the <general> defaults that reach the position/velocity actuator shortcuts), and derives the ten actuator control ranges, the joint dimensions and the option time step from the same text. It loads no mesh, resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint, and integrates a placeholder motion toward each control value instead of MuJoCo's dynamics; the fidelity gaps list every difference. The real mujoco path (backend sim) was not run here.

NOT COVERED: the camera RGB and depth arrays and the 2D lidar scan are NOT COVERED: the standard's world capabilities carry no camera or scan array and this driver exposes only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state, not the upstream StretchMujocoSimulator camera, sensor or joint-status API. MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; there is no rendering, no mesh or texture loading, and no physical Stretch is modelled. Nothing was validated against the hardware. The fake returns the full model qpos/qvel dimensions, not a reduced array.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the integer/numeric inputs the simulator family derives and that the authoring guide's expected-warning list calls expected. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised, and G1-G5, G9 passed.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card scene, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control target, reset, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1. No operator_required limit: the model file is the system of record for the control envelope.
